title: Quantification of sugars and organic acids in tomato fruits
author: Agius, von Tucher, et al.

steps.title: Prepare tomato extract
steps.instruction: Homogenise ~100 g tomato fruits with an Ultra‑Turrax or Warring Blender, transfer homogenate to 50 ml tubes and centrifuge at 4000 g for 5 min; filter the supernatant through Miracloth (paper filter optional), then filter ~2 ml of the filtrate through a 0.22 µm syringe filter (PP, nylon or hydrophilic PTFE). Store filtrate at –20 °C if not used immediately. Transfer exactly 25 ml of filtrate into a beaker on an analytical balance, weigh and calculate density (weight/volume). The density step is optional if only concentrations (g l⁻¹) are required.

steps.title: Add internal standards and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Transfer exactly 400 µl of the extract into a 1.5 ml reaction tube, add 100 µl tricarballylic acid (10 g l⁻¹, internal standard for organic acids), 100 µl lactose (100 g l⁻¹, internal standard for sugars) and 400 µl acetonitrile (ACN) 100 %; centrifuge at >10 000 rpm for 5 min.

steps.title: Equilibrate NH₂ SPE column
steps.instruction: Equilibrate a Chromabond 100 mg NH₂ column sequentially with 1 ml ACN 100 % and then 1 ml ACN 40 %.

steps.title: Load sample and collect flow‑through (sugars)
steps.instruction: Load the diluted sample (total 1000 µl) onto the equilibrated SPE column and allow it to flow through by gravity; wash the column with 1 ml ACN 40 %; apply vacuum at 400 mbar for 30 s. Collect the combined flow‑through and wash solution, which contains the sugars; store this solution in the dark at room temperature for up to one month.

steps.title: Elute organic acids
steps.instruction: Place a fresh collection tube in the SPE apparatus, load 1000 µl of 400 mM phosphoric acid (for HPLC) **or** 1000 µl of 400 mM trifluoroacetic acid (for GC‑MS) onto the column, apply gentle vacuum (~700 mbar) to draw the solution through, then let the eluate run by gravity. Finally, apply vacuum at 400 mbar to collect the entire eluate. Store the eluate at –20 °C for up to one month before analysis (only phosphoric‑acid eluates are suitable for RP‑HPLC).

steps.title: Prepare sugar samples for HPLC
steps.instruction: Transfer 200 µl of the sugar‑containing flow‑through into an autosampler vial, add 800 µl ACN 90 % and mix well. Perform this step at a temperature >25 °C to avoid phase separation.

steps.title: Prepare sugar standards
steps.instruction:
Prepare the following standard mixes (volumes in µl) as shown in Table 1, then transfer 200 µl of each mix into autosampler vials and add 800 µl ACN 90 %; mix well and keep the temperature >25 °C.
Table 1 (standard composition):
- St 1: Lactose 1000, H₂O 1400, ACN 1000
- St 2: Lactose 100, H₂O 1360, ACN 1000
- St 3: Lactose 80, H₂O 1320, ACN 1000
- St 4: Lactose 120, H₂O 100, ACN 1280, ACN 1000
- St 5: Lactose 160, H₂O 100, ACN 1240, ACN 1000
- St 6: Lactose 200, H₂O 100, ACN 1200, ACN 1000
- St 7: Lactose 300, H₂O 100, ACN 1100, ACN 1000
- St 8: Lactose 400, H₂O 100, ACN 1000, ACN 1000

steps.title: Run sugar HPLC analysis
steps.instruction: Inject samples on a Nucleodur 100‑5 NH₂ column (125 × 4 mm) with a 4 × 3 mm precolumn, using 80 % ACN as eluent at 1.0 ml min⁻¹, column oven at 30 °C, full‑loop injection with a 100 µl loop, RI detection, total run time ≈18 min.

steps.title: Prepare organic‑acid samples for RP‑HPLC
steps.instruction: Transfer the phosphoric‑acid eluate into an autosampler vial and close the lid (only eluates obtained with 400 mM phosphoric acid are suitable for RP‑HPLC).

steps.title: Prepare organic‑acid standards
steps.instruction:
Prepare the following standard mixes (volumes in µl) as shown in Table 2, then place each mix into autosampler vials. For GC‑MS analysis replace phosphoric acid with 400 mM TFA.
Table 2 (standard composition):
- St 1: Tricarballylic acid 100, Water 80, Phosphoric acid 100
- St 2: Tricarballylic acid 200, Water 100, Phosphoric acid 78, 100
- St 3: Tricarballylic acid 350, Water 100, Phosphoric acid 75, 100
- St 4: Tricarballylic acid 410, Water 100, Phosphoric acid 70, 100
- St 5: Tricarballylic acid 520, Water 100, Phosphoric acid 60, 100
- St 6: Tricarballylic acid 640, Water 100, Phosphoric acid 40, 100
- St 7: Tricarballylic acid 760, Water 100, Phosphoric acid 20, 100
- St 8: Tricarballylic acid 880, Water 100, Phosphoric acid 0, 100

steps.title: Run organic‑acid RP‑HPLC analysis
steps.instruction:
Inject 25 µl of each sample on a Nucleodur 100‑5 C18ec column (250 × 4 mm) with a 4 × 3 mm precolumn, column oven at 25 °C, flow 0.6 ml min⁻¹, UV detection at 210 nm. Apply the gradient described in Table 3:
- 0 min: 100 % A, 0 % B
- 1 min: 66.5 % A, 33.5 % B
- 2 min: 52 % A, 48 % B
- 10 min: 18 % A, 82 % B
- 25 min: 0 % A, 100 % B
Acids elute within the first 16 min; the remainder of the run flushes and re‑equilibrates the column.
